doc: The shared oracle for the ONE drawn predicate: does this turn draw a card, and therefore
does the rail hold a row for it. The server half is internal/chat's drawnBy (asked through
EntryLog.RailRows) and the client half is static-src/turns.ts turnIsDrawn; each reader builds
its own rows from these cases, which is the disagreement the fixture exists to catch.
owner is per case because one clause has no server twin: an open entry never reaches the log,
so a client-only case is skipped by the Go reader and every skip is counted, or a reader that
silently ignored rows would read as agreement.
body lists every entry after the turn_open, in order, including the turn_close where the case
has one. lane is "" for the turn's own agent and a delegate uuid otherwise.
The plans clause is deliberately UNASSERTED. Both halves refuse a plan that is not the turn's
first, and neither refusal can change a turn-level verdict: the first lane-"" plan draws the
turn, so a later one is only ever reached on a turn already drawn. A shape that would separate
them (a delegate-lane plan before a lane-"" one) is not produced by any writer -- turnlog's
Turn.Plan appends laneless and the replay projection emits no plan at all -- so asserting it
would pin a divergence over an input nothing can send.

cases.name: a prompt turn draws on its header alone
a local_shell turn draws on its header alone
an empty_retry turn draws on its header alone
an agent-initiated turn with an empty body draws nothing
a bind renders at no position of its own
a tool_result is charged at its tool_call and draws nothing itself
an ack-only turn IS drawn, because an ack is agent words at its own position
the turn's first plan draws it
a delegate lane's prose draws no turn in the issuer's view
the invocation in the issuer's lane draws the turn its delegate runs in
a laned ack draws nothing, because it renders in the delegate's own view
a reconciled record renders at no position of its own
a turn_revert draws the turn carrying it, because it IS the boundary row
an open entry in lane "" draws the turn it is streaming into
